description: Two spouses' Schedule C businesses, each its own § 199A business (replaces the old refusal). MFJ, W-2 wages $300,000, each spouse $100,000 of profit. Half-SE: taxpayer $1,339 (Medicare only — their W-2 filled the wage base), spouse $7,065. QBI: main $98,661, spouse $92,935. Taxable income before QBI $491,596 − $31,500 = $460,096; excess over $394,600 = $65,496 of the $100,000 range. Main (not an SSTB, no W-2 wages): 20% = $19,732.20, less $19,732.20 × 65,496/100,000 = $12,923.80 → $6,808.40. Spouse (SSTB): applicable percentage 34.504% → QBI $32,066.29, 20% = $6,413.26, less $4,200.43 → $2,212.83. Total $9,021.23; overall limit $92,019.20.
